title: Southeast Asia's Best Marathons and Half Marathons
seo_title: Southeast Asia's Best Marathons and Half Marathons, by the Data
meta_description: The region's biggest, fastest and most distinctive marathons and half marathons, picked from official results for 238,000 finishers rather than from reputation.
dek: Picked from official results rather than reputation: which marathons and half marathons draw the biggest fields, where the fast times are run, and which races are worth the trip for the course itself.

sections.heading: What 238,000 finishers show
paragraphs: Our results archive holds the latest edition of 75 Southeast Asian road races: 238,642 finishers across the marathon, half marathon and 10K [1]. Across 25 marathons (30,732 finishers) the median finish is 5:25, one finisher in ten takes longer than 6:54, and 11% break four hours. Across 74 half marathons (111,805 finishers) the median is 2:42 and 12% break two hours [1].
Women are 18% of marathon finishers and 29% of half-marathon finishers. At 10K they are close to half the field, at 47% [1].

The country a race is in matters more than any one course. Vietnam's four marathons have a combined median of 4:41, with 26% of finishers under four hours. Thailand's two come in at 5:09, Singapore's at 5:16 and Indonesia's two at 5:26. The Philippines' 15 marathons have a median of 5:49, with 5% under four hours. Malaysia's one marathon in the sample has the slowest median, at 5:58. Half-marathon medians run from 2:23 in Thailand to 2:54 in Malaysia [1].

Of the 446 races in our calendar, 349 are dated between August and December, which is when most of the big city races are held [3]. The picks below are based on the size of each race's latest field in our results, on what the times say about the course and the conditions, and on whether the organiser publishes its cut-offs. There are no scores. Some well-known races have no full results in our archive, such as the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon and the Penang Bridge race, so they're covered in the country guides instead.

sections.heading: The three biggest race days: Singapore, Bangkok and Manila
paragraphs: Singapore's marathon has the largest marathon field in our data: 9,294 finishers in the December 2025 edition, plus 14,817 in the half [1]. The median marathon was 5:16, and 12% of finishers broke four hours. The 2026 race weekend runs from 4 to 6 December, with a 7-hour limit for the marathon and 3 hours 45 for the half [4]. In 2025, 6.4% of marathon finishers took longer than 7 hours, so runners near the back of the field should plan around that limit [1]. Its race page is at runsea.run/race/byd-singapore-international-marathon-by-adidas/.

The Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok had the largest half marathon we hold: 17,770 finishers in 2025, alongside 5,837 in the marathon [2]. Its marathon median of 4:54, with 20% under four hours, is quick for a field that size. The organiser puts attendance at more than 48,000 runners a year. The marathon starts at 2am from Sanam Luang. The route passes Victory Monument, the Rama VIII Bridge, the Golden Mountain and the Grand Palace area, and the limits are 7 hours for the marathon and 3.5 hours for the half [5].

Manila has grown faster than any race we track. The Manila Marathon had 431 marathon finishers in October 2024, 2,827 in August 2025 and 5,744 in June 2026, plus 9,291 in the half [1][2]. Its field is also the slowest of the big three, with a median of 5:58, 3% under four hours, and one finisher in ten past 7:29 [1]. That suits a newer runner: the organiser allows 8 hours for the marathon and 4 for the half, with an 11.30pm marathon start [6].

sections.heading: Indonesia: Borobudur and Bali
paragraphs: The Borobudur Marathon starts and finishes at Taman Lumbini in the Borobudur temple complex in Central Java. Its 2025 route was changed to run through villages, with the Menoreh hills as a backdrop [7]. That edition had 3,603 marathon finishers, with a median of 5:32, and 3,640 in the half, 40% of them women. That is one of the highest female shares for a half marathon of that size [2]. Its race page is at runsea.run/race/bank-jateng-borobudur-marathon-2026/.

The Maybank Marathon in Bali, which held its 15th edition in 2026 [8], had almost the same size of marathon field: 3,578 finishers, with a median of 5:26 and 8% under four hours. It also had 5,219 finishers in the half [1]. The course runs through Gianyar's villages rather than a city, so it's a different kind of race from the capitals [3].

sections.heading: Vietnam: where the fast times are
paragraphs: If a fast time is the goal, the numbers point north. The Ha Long Bay Heritage Marathon had 2,579 marathon finishers in 2025, with a median of 4:08 and 46% under four hours, the fastest marathon field in our archive [2]. The organiser describes a coastal route on Ha Long Bay, a UNESCO-recognised natural heritage site, and expects about 18,000 runners across all distances in 2026 [9].

Hanoi has two big marathons in October. The VPBank Hanoi International Marathon had 1,844 marathon finishers and a 4:35 median, with 28% under four hours. The Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon had 1,975 finishers and a 4:43 median [1]. Techcombank's field has grown from 1,110 marathon finishers in 2024 [2]. VPBank starts at Hoan Kiem Lake, but its 6-hour marathon limit and 3.5 hours for the half are tighter than most in the region [10].

For a fast half marathon, Thailand's provincial races beat the capitals. Naew Ubon Run had 750 half-marathon finishers with a median of 2:15, and 32% of them broke two hours. Udon21's median was 2:10 [1].

sections.heading: The longest track records: Pattaya and Laguna Phuket
paragraphs: The Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon has run since 1993 and held its 33rd edition in September 2026. It allows 7 hours for the marathon and 3.5 for the half, and it adds a 4.5 km family run the day before [11].

Our records for the Laguna Phuket Marathon go back to 2019, and they show how far a field can fall. Marathon finishers dropped from 2,231 in 2019 to 1,049 in 2022 and 603 in 2026. Half-marathon finishers fell from 3,689 to 1,737 [1][2]. The race itself has kept a generous 7.5-hour marathon limit with intermediate checkpoints, a 4-hour half and a 2 km junior run on the Saturday [12]. A smaller field and a resort start and finish make it a calm marathon. Its race page is at runsea.run/race/laguna-phuket-marathon-2027/.

sections.heading: Singapore beyond the marathon, and what the numbers can't tell you
paragraphs: Singapore's other half marathons are small but quick. Garmin Run Singapore had 3,082 half-marathon finishers in 2025, with a median of 2:25 and 19% under two hours, which is faster than the marathon weekend's half [1]. The Kiprun Singapore drew 5,342 finishers to its 10K [1]. The calendar is fragile, though: two of Singapore's 2026 half marathons, the JomRun-powered Singapore Half Marathon and the Great Eastern Women's Run, were cancelled [3].

Each figure here comes from one edition, and it counts finishers, not entrants. A hot morning slows a whole field, and a change of date can shrink one. A slow median isn't a mark against a race either: Manila's tells you it welcomes newer runners. The country guides go deeper on Malaysia (runsea.run/articles/best-marathons-half-marathons-malaysia/), the Philippines (runsea.run/articles/best-marathons-half-marathons-philippines/), Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam. For a first race, see runsea.run/articles/best-races-first-marathon-half-marathon-southeast-asia/.

faqs.question: What is the biggest marathon in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: By finishers in our results archive, the Singapore marathon is the biggest, with 9,294 finishers in its December 2025 edition. Bangkok (5,837 in 2025) and Manila (5,744 in June 2026) come next. The largest half marathon we hold is Bangkok's, with 17,770 finishers in 2025.

faqs.question: Where are the fastest marathons in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: In Vietnam. The Ha Long Bay Heritage Marathon's 2025 field had a median of 4:08, with 46% of finishers under four hours. Hanoi's two October marathons had medians of 4:35 and 4:43. Across all 25 marathons in our data, the median is 5:25.

faqs.question: Which big Southeast Asian marathons have the most generous time limits?
faqs.answer: Manila allows 8 hours and Laguna Phuket 7.5 hours. Singapore, Bangkok and Pattaya allow 7 hours. VPBank Hanoi is tighter, at 6 hours. Organisers can change limits from year to year, so check the current race information before you enter.

editorial_notes: Picks are based on Run SEA's own results archive (latest edition of 75 races, plus earlier editions for 35) and race calendar, together with organisers' published race information checked on 6 Nov 2026. World Athletics label tiers are deliberately not given, because they could not be checked against the current World Athletics label list. This is not a sponsored ranking.
